Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |

| Secuura/Blockchain s168 (`%3`, 2026-09-10 13:26 → 14:06 AEST — the kintsugi seat: measured a deploy nobody had scoped, and stopped twice) | **IT USED THE MARGIN CLAUSE CORRECTLY AND THEN FOUND TWO THINGS THAT CHANGED THE PLAN.** 🔴 **THERE IS NO ROLLBACK ON THAT BOX AT ALL** — 31/31 images tagged bare `:latest`, **ZERO dangling**, no script or previous-image record anywhere, **so a build overwrites `:latest` and nobody records the old IDs.** Rollback today = rebuilding from old source, **~1.5 hours.** ✅ **And the fix costs SECONDS: re-tag all 31 as `:pre-<date>` before building** — a tag is a pointer, not a copy — turning rollback into **31 `docker tag` + one restart, ~2 minutes.** Corollary it wrote in bold: **no `docker prune`, image OR builder, at any point** — the 29 GB cache is the only rollback material that exists. 🔑 **AND ITS ORDERING DISSOLVED WEDNESDAY'S OWN OBJECTION TO KAM.** Wednesday had argued against an overnight run because *"a half-rebuilt estate is worse than a stale one"*. **`docker build` is non-destructive**, so: tag → rsync → **build all 31 with NOTHING SWAPPED (a failure there is FREE)** → migrations → swap one at a time. **The dangerous window drops from ~90 minutes to about two**, and Wednesday amended the card rather than let Kam rule on a stale risk picture. ✅ **MIGRATION ORDER SETTLED ON A MECHANISM, NOT A PRINCIPLE — it read all five rather than reasoning from the general case:** 046 and 047 add CHECK constraints, and **047's own comment records the `POST /api/oauth/apps {"appType":"native"}` that used to return 201** — old code demonstrably writes outside the set, so migrations-first turns a silent success into a violation. **And migrations-LAST is also wrong** (044 adds five columns new code expects). ⚠ **It carried the limit that none of the five ships a down-migration**, so a full rollback leaves old code under the new constraints — written as an **escalation, not a mid-flight decision.** 🟠 **A SCOPE FINDING IT REFUSED TO DECIDE: demo RUNS `guardian` and `queue`; kintsugi has NEITHER — no container AND no image.** *"Bring kintsugi up to date" does not say whether it means match develop or match demo, and those differ by two services.* It recommended including them and **named that this widens Kam's authorisation, so it is not its call.** And it spotted that **trap 2 is inert today and goes LIVE the moment they exist** — compose treats both as orphans, so `--remove-orphans` would delete them. ✅ **The revision defect measured and a fix PROPOSED not implemented:** no `.git`, no marker, **31/31 images with no SHA label** — demo identical — with the observation that **the label travels with the artefact, so a partially-updated box says so per-image instead of averaging.** | 1 | **1.00** |
